newsitem.title: FRANCE: De Silguy says more Italy deficit cutting possible.
newsitem.headline: De Silguy says more Italy deficit cutting possible.

text.p: European monetary affairs Commissioner Yves Thibault de Silguy said on Friday it was possible for Italy to maintain its deficit-cutting efforts beyond 1997.
Asked in a television interview on LCI whether Italy's deficit cutting efforts could be sustainable, de Silguy replied, "It is feasible".

On Monday, EU finance ministers in Brussels approved a sharply worded Commission report on the state of Italy's finances suggesting that many of the measures taken recently to slash its budget deficit were not sustainable.
He added that further efforts were indispensable since it would be unacceptable for countries to have their deficits slip back over three percent of gross domestic product from 1998.

"The Italians are going to cut their public deficits this year three times as much as the Germans and the French, they are making considerable progress and efforts, but I am not able to say today whether it will be enough," De Silguy said.
